one_line: Greco-Bactrian frontier kings pioneering rare cupro‑nickel coinage on the Oxus–India routes.

appearance.age_look: Late 20s to mid‑30s, athletic but not bulky, the composed bearing of educated warrior‑kings.
appearance.face: Classically Greek oval faces with straight noses and strong chins, lightly tanned Central Asian complexions, neatly groomed short beards; Agathocles’ default expression is calm, analytical focus, while Pantaleon’s is a faint, confident half‑smile.
appearance.hair: Both have dark brown, wavy hair cut short in a Hellenistic style; Agathocles keeps it slightly shorter and tidier with a narrow gold fillet band, Pantaleon’s is a little more tousled with a soft leather headband in dark red.
appearance.costume: They wear Hellenistic military‑court dress adapted to Bactria: knee‑length white wool chitons under short, fitted Macedonian‑style tunics in muted teal with narrow dark red borders, belted with brown leather girdles; over this, each has a light grey‑blue wool chlamys cloak pinned at the right shoulder with a simple bronze brooch, the cloaks’ edges trimmed in a thin dark blue stripe; they both have fitted, ankle‑length sandy‑brown trousers (in the Iranian–Central Asian style) tucked into mid‑calf brown leather boots; Agathocles’ tunic hem bears a subtle meander pattern in dull gold thread, while Pantaleon’s shows a row of tiny stylised spear motifs; both wear modest Hellenistic rings and a single small, round bronze pendant engraved with a coin motif, avoiding ostentatious jewellery to keep a practical, frontier‑court look.
appearance.signature: A shallow, round bronze coin‑maker’s tray cradled in Agathocles’ arm, holding a few gleaming cupro‑nickel coins, and in Pantaleon’s hand a short, iron striking hammer with a wooden handle and a separate engraved coin die, their shared signature prop symbolising their metallurgical innovation rather than battlefield weapons.

ref_desc: Agathocles and Pantaleon are two late‑20s Greco‑Bactrian kings with short wavy dark brown hair, light tans, trimmed beards, wearing white chitons, muted teal tunics, grey‑blue cloaks, sandy‑brown trousers and brown boots, holding a bronze coin tray, hammer and die, accented in dark red and dull gold.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style model sheet of two Greco‑Bactrian frontier kings, Agathocles and Pantaleon, standing side by side in a realistic 2nd century BCE Bactrian setting: both in their late 20s with athletic builds, lightly tanned complexions, classically Greek features, straight noses and short trimmed beards; each has short, wavy dark brown hair, Agathocles’ slightly neater with a narrow gold fillet, Pantaleon’s a bit more tousled with a dark red leather headband. Dress them in historically plausible Hellenistic military‑court clothing adapted to Central Asia: knee‑length white wool chitons under short fitted muted teal tunics with narrow dark red borders, belted with brown leather girdles; over these, drape light grey‑blue wool chlamys cloaks pinned at the right shoulder with simple bronze brooches, the cloak edges finished with a thin dark blue stripe. Give both fitted, ankle‑length sandy‑brown trousers in an Iranian‑style cut tucked into mid‑calf brown leather boots; decorate Agathocles’ tunic hem with a subtle dull‑gold meander pattern, and Pantaleon’s with a line of tiny stylised spear motifs. Keep jewellery modest: simple rings and a single small round bronze pendant engraved with a coin design. Place a shallow round bronze coin‑maker’s tray in Agathocles’ arm with a few gleaming pale cupro‑nickel coins visible, and in Pantaleon’s hand a short iron striking hammer with a wooden handle and a separate small engraved die, clearly their key props instead of weapons. Use a restrained palette dominated by white, muted teal, dark red accents, grey‑blue, sandy brown and dull gold details, and show them front‑facing with calm, dignified expressions, suitable for consistent redrawing in many panels.
